title: Decision Trees
outcome: By the end, I can fit a one-question tree using training labels and an explicit candidate comparison.
scenario: A fictional toy classifier predicts whether a book needs an illustration label.
given: Candidates ask colour_cover or diagram_inside; each leaf uses its training majority. A leaf tie chooses No. Select fewer training errors.

steps.label: Colour candidate
steps.detail: Both colour leaves tie Yes/No, choose No: two training errors.

steps.label: Diagram candidate
steps.detail: Diagram 1 leaf predicts Yes; diagram 0 leaf predicts No: zero errors.

steps.label: Select tree
steps.detail: Choose the diagram question using the training comparison.

steps.label: Apply new input
steps.detail: A new (1,0) row follows diagram=0 and predicts No.

explanation: A question becomes a fitted tree only after its leaves and selection procedure are specified. The training comparison prefers the feature that separates these labels. Prediction follows the selected question; it does not reselect the tree using a new case’s answer. Save candidate leaves and errors so the choice can be repeated.

counterfactual.reason: It follows diagram=1; cover colour is not the selected question.

student_task: Why does changing colour alone not change this tree’s prediction?
teacher_answer: The fitted tree branches only on diagram_inside; colour was considered but not selected.
project_evidence: Fit or hand-specify recommender classification rules transparently, retaining candidate definitions and training-only selection evidence.
limits: Zero errors on four toy examples do not establish that diagrams always determine a real book’s classification.
review_note: New fictional case individually matched to this topic, with computations and policy traces checked. Use for supported practice; preserve the independent assessment.
